findings.title: The server requires credentials but advertises no MCP OAuth challenge
findings.message: The endpoint requires authorization but presented no MCP OAuth challenge: its response carried no WWW-Authenticate header. MCP authorization is OPTIONAL, so this is not a violation — the server may authenticate through a non-OAuth scheme such as an API key or a static bearer token, which the MCP authorization specification does not cover and which this scanner cannot audit for OAuth conformance. It does mean a client that only supports zero-configuration OAuth discovery cannot connect.
findings.fix: If the server uses MCP OAuth, return 401 with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge carrying a resource_metadata pointer. If it authenticates with an API key or static token, no change is needed — but zero-configuration OAuth clients will not be able to connect.

prm.error: Error: HTTP 401 trying to load well-known OAuth protected resource metadata.
